2026-10-08T23:09:50.2262927Z 
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2264268Z For multiple or complex arguments, pass the JSON object inline as a single quoted argument — the binary comes first, so a malformed command still runs the CLI and reports an error:
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2265546Z ```bash
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2266136Z safeoutputs add_comment '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}'
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2266853Z ```
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2267685Z Alternatively, pipe a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel (prefer this only for large bodies built from files):
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2268649Z ```bash
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2269267Z printf '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}' | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2270193Z # or read from a file: safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2270896Z ```
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2272006Z When piping, make sure the `|` is actually present: `printf '{...}' safeoutputs add_comment .` (no pipe) prints the JSON and exits 0 without ever running the CLI, so nothing is emitted.
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2273473Z 
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2277294Z **Multi-line or long `body` content:** do NOT build the JSON payload with `printf`/`echo` embedding raw newlines or many escaped characters directly in the command line — the sandbox's shell command-injection guard may reject long or complex quoted arguments (reporting "expansion patterns"/"command substitution" even though none are present) and retrying the identical command will fail again. Instead, write the content to a temp file with a heredoc, then use `jq -Rs` to inject it as the `body` field:
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2280243Z ```bash
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2280657Z cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gh-aw/body.md
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2281158Z Title
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2281380Z 
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2281595Z Multi-line body content goes here.
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2282098Z EOF
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2282713Z jq -Rs '{title: "My title", body: .}' /tmp/gh-aw/body.md | safeoutputs create_discussion .
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2283650Z ```
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2286218Z If a shell command is rejected for containing expansion patterns, do not retry the same command — switch to the heredoc + `jq -Rs` pattern above.
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2287157Z 
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2287775Z To inject an entire local file as the `body` field without re-embedding its content in the model context, use `jq -Rs`:
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2288696Z ```bash
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2289181Z jq -Rs --arg discussion_number "$DISCUSSION_NUMBER" \
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2289992Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2290678Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2291201Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2291718Z ```
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2292985Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
2026-10-08T23:09:50.2294420Z
